title: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found
body:
Read the chapter → [Job 28](/bible/job/28)

**[Job 28:1-6](/bible/job/28#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/job/28#v1)</sup> Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/job/28#v2)</sup> Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/job/28#v3)</sup> He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/job/28#v4)</sup> The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/job/28#v5)</sup> As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/job/28#v6)</sup> The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.

- Surely there is a vein for the silver and a place for gold where they find it, iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone; Job speaks of the elements that are in the earth.
- He setteth an end to darkness and searcheth out all perfection, the stones of darkness and the shadow of death.
- The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant, even the waters forgotten of the foot are dried up and gone away from men; out of the earth cometh bread, like wheat, and under it is turned up as it were fire.
- The stones of the earth are the place of sapphires and it hath dust of gold; the precepts in Job are very parabolistic, full of parables, similitudes, and double meanings, so Job is a hard book to take straight off the top.

**[Job 28:7-11](/bible/job/28#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/job/28#v7)</sup> There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/job/28#v8)</sup> The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/job/28#v9)</sup> He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/job/28#v10)</sup> He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/job/28#v11)</sup> He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.

- There is a path which no fowl knoweth and which the vulture's eye hath not seen, the lion's whelps have not trodden it nor the fierce lion passed by it.
- He putteth forth his hand upon the rock and overturneth the mountains by the roots, he cutteth out rivers among the rocks, and his eye seeth every precious thing.
- He bindeth the floods from overflowing and bringeth the thing that is hid forth to light.

**[Job 28:12-19](/bible/job/28#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/job/28#v12)</sup> But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/job/28#v13)</sup> Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/job/28#v14)</sup> The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/job/28#v15)</sup> It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/job/28#v16)</sup> It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/job/28#v17)</sup> The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/job/28#v18)</sup> No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/job/28#v19)</sup> The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

- Where shall wisdom be found and where is the place of understanding; man knoweth not the price thereof, neither is it found in the land of the living.
- The depth saith it is not in me and the sea saith it is not with me; it cannot be gotten for gold nor silver weighed for its price, nor valued with the gold of Ophir, the onyx, or the sapphire.
- The gold and the crystal cannot equal it, no mention shall be made of coral or pearls, for the price of wisdom is above rubies; you will not find God's wisdom deep in the roots of Wakanda, there is no price you can give for it.
- To get the wisdom of the Most High you take heed to his commandments; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, understanding that the Lord created us, made us, and can take us out.
- Everything is in steps, including wisdom; the fear of the Lord is the first step to being accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
  - **[Psalms 111:10](/bible/psalms/111#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/111#v10)</sup> The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.

    The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 19:18-20](/bible/sirach/19#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/sirach/19#v18)</sup> The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/sirach/19#v19)</sup> The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/sirach/19#v20)</sup> The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

    The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

**[Job 28:20-28](/bible/job/28#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/job/28#v20)</sup> Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/job/28#v21)</sup> Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/job/28#v22)</sup> Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/job/28#v23)</sup> God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/job/28#v24)</sup> For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/job/28#v25)</sup> To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/job/28#v26)</sup> When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/job/28#v27)</sup> Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/job/28#v28)</sup> And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

- Whence then cometh wisdom and where is the place of understanding; it is hid from the eyes of all living and kept close from the fowls of the air.
- Destruction and death say they have heard the fame thereof with their ears, but God understandeth the way thereof and knoweth the place thereof, for he looketh to the ends of the earth and seeth under the whole heaven.
- He maketh the weight for the winds and weigheth the waters by measure, he made a decree for the rain and a way for the lightning of the thunder, then he saw it, declared it, prepared it, and searched it out.
- Unto man he said, behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding; Job breaks it down, wisdom is the fear of the Lord and understanding is to depart from evil.
- Wisdom and understanding are hid from all living and given only to the few, the remnant of Israel who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations; we fear the Lord like King David, the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who still trembled at God's judgments.
  - **[2 Esdras 8:62](/bible/2-esdras/8#v62)**
    > <sup>[62](/bible/2-esdras/8#v62)</sup> These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee. Then answered I and said,

    These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee; the wisdom and understanding of the Lord is for the remnant, not the heathen.
  - **[Psalms 119:120](/bible/psalms/119#v120)**
    > <sup>[120](/bible/psalms/119#v120)</sup> My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.

    My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments; even King David, who taught his hands to war and could leap a wall, feared the Lord.
  - **[Psalms 1:4](/bible/psalms/1#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/1#v4)</sup> The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

    The ungodly are like the chaff which the wind driveth away, tied to the wind of destruction in Job 27, the nuclear destruction and the winds held back in Revelation.
